steps.text: Bring sugar and corn syrup to a boil in a saucepan over medium heat.
Stir in butter and peanut butter until thoroughly combined, then remove from the heat.
Place cornflakes into a large bowl. Pour peanut butter mixture over top and mix until cornflakes are well coated.
Drop 1-tablespoon scoops of the mixture onto a waxed-paper lined baking sheet. Flatten slightly if desired, then allow to cool for 30 minutes before serving.

raw_recipe.headline: Grama's Cornflake Peanut Butter Cookies
raw_recipe.description: These peanut butter cornflake cookies are easy to make for a sweet treat! Once the sugar mixture has boiled, your kids can help with the rest!
raw_recipe.name: Grama's Cornflake Peanut Butter Cookies

review.reviewBody: Simple and quick - the perfect go to recipe when you need a little treat! I also make these with 1/2 cup butterscotch chips & 1/2 cup peanut butter melted together and 3 cups of corn flakes.

Great Recipe! Mine came out wonderful!

I made one change. I used maple syrup instead of corn syrup. I also put them in the fridge when I was done putting them into individual cookies so they were ready faster. I also didn't have an wax paper but a plastic cutting board worked just fine.

I learned to make a version of these in fourth grade, but the recipe I knew was slightly different. It had 1/2 cup each of sugar and light Karo, but no butter and a whole cup of peanut butter, and then used 6 cups of cornflakes. Those were less sweet than this version would be.

I have been making these for over 60 yrs. Only difference is the amts & no butter. (May try that though) 1 cup Karo Syrup 1 cup Sugar Bring to boil & remove from heat. Stir in 1 cup Peanut Butter Add 6 cups of corn flakes & spoon out on parchment paper. 😋

A very forgiving recipe which produces a favorite public school dessert from the 70's. I have stopped using corn syrup but the results are the same

I used:
 agave nectar 1 cup
1/2 cup sugar
3 TBSP butter and brought to a boil for 1 min 
removed from heat and added a heaping cup of peanut butter stirring until smooth. added 8 cups of corn flakes (no need to crush) Stir until mixed
poured all into a buttered 11x7 glass x dish. smash down with bottom of pan or glass.
Takes a couple of hours to harden enough to hold together. Cut into squares. Try not to eat the whole pan by yourself!!

these were great after a few adjustments, made a trial batch, and they were OK, but seemed like it needed more peanut butter to get that better P.B. taste, tried it again a while later but I cut back on the sugar (down to 1/3 cup) and used sugar frosted flakes, then increased the peanut butter by 1/3 cup , in addition I tried letting the mixture cool in the bowl about 5 mins, then added some M&M s to it , ( just before the mixture started to set) and mixed well so I got some chocolate flavoring as well as P.B. They were so good, had two others ask for the recipe

I remember these from my childhood. This was really easy and took so few ingredients. My butter was unsalted, so I did add a few twists of salt to compensate. The hardest part of this was waiting half an hour for them to set so we could eat them. I used creamy peanut butter and did add a little more than called for as I didn't level the cup. It had a nice peanut butter flavor but they were really sweet. They set up nicely and weren't sticky at all even though the syrup was still a little soft and bendy and they were stringy when you pulled them apart the same way a Rice Krispie Treat is. There was just the right amount of syrup to corn flakes. These were like I remember and so easy to do and best of all, no heating up the kitchen with the oven when it's already hot outside. I feel like drizzling these with a bit of semisweet chocolate would finish them off and make them pretty for a treat tray. This makes a small batch of only 2 dozen cookies.
My Grandmother and I used to make these in the late 80"s and 90's. I love love love them. Our only difference is we used only peanutbutter and no butter.

Loved this it was fast and easy to make! I was looking for a sweet treat using only stuff I had on hand! This made the cut! I did add a couple things to it. I added 2 Tbs cocoa powder (because I had it and my family loves chocolate) and 1/2 tsp vanilla. These came out great! I will be making these again!

I have made these for 50 years and my mom and grandma made them before me. I have never added butter. I do add extra peanut butter. I have used Corn Chex instead of corn flakes and never had any left. Both work well with the recipe.

Wow, these are delicious! (I'm making them for my parents, at 3:30 AM!) I had to use maple syrup and brown sugar since it's all I had on hand, but they turned out just fine. I've also mixed a bit of salt to the sugar, and sprinkled some cinnamon as an extra touch. Thank you for sharing!
Best no bake cookie ever

I made them because I thought I found some leftover crumbs in a container after Christmas. I didn't get to try a whole cookie. Mine came out soso they were rock hard not easy to eat. I'm going to try them again probably with the maple syrup. Or some butter scotch chips

When I saw the recipe I knew I had to make them. It reminded me of when I was a kid and my mom would make them. So good. I did add some chocolate granola to mine just because I needed to use it up and thought it would go good with this classic recipe. Other than that they are great tasting just they way they are. ☺️
Love these and easy to make! My children make them disappear.

I preheated the oven to 350 and cooked half a batch about 7 minutes before I realized that these aren’t supposed to get cooked. Now I have two versions of the same recipe. Both good. However not recommended for diabetics.
Easy, Good, and everyone likes them
Delicious and easy
This is a great and easy recipe! They’re so good I can’t stop eating them! This is definitely a keeper!
These cookies are amazing. The only problem I found with them is that I can't stop eating them.
